stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan crosses Andhra Pradesh coast near Gopalpur after weakening
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan crosses Andhra Pradesh coast near Gopalpur after weakening
stories.summary: Cyclonic Storm Akvan crossed the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts near Gopalpur on Friday after weakening from a severe cyclonic storm. Authorities reported no damage, while residents of Srikakulam were advised to remain alert as rain remained likely.
reasons: source: event has 4 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence

opening: Cyclonic Storm Akvan crossed the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts near Gopalpur on Friday after weakening from a severe cyclonic storm.
Authorities reported no damage, while residents of Srikakulam were advised to remain alert as rain remained likely.
body: Visakhapatnam, Nov 20: Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’ crossed north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur on Friday, the IMD said, adding that the severe cyclonic storm has weakened into a cyclonic storm before making landfall.

India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in a bulletin that ‘Akvan’ over the westcentral Bay of Bengal near north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts moved north-northwestwards with the speed of 26 kmph during the past six hours and crossed the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur with a wind speed of 70-80kmph gusting to 90kmph during 0730-0830 IST.
It is likely to move nearly north-northeastwards across Odisha and weaken into a deep depression during the next three hours and into a depression during the subsequent six hours, it said.
According to the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA), light to moderate rain is likely in North Andhra.

Even though the system has crossed the coast, residents of Srikakulam district must remain alert, said Prakhar Jain, Managing Director of APSDMA and Chief Executive Officer of Real Time Governance Society (RTGS).
Authorities in Andhra Pradesh heaved a sigh of relief as ‘Akvan’ weakened before making landfall.
There are no reports of any damage from anywhere.
This was the third cyclone to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast in less than a month.
Very severe cyclonic storm ‘Arnab’ had struck the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 27.
Severe cyclonic storm ‘Murasu’ had crossed the coast between Nellore and Narasapur on November 3.
Two cyclones within a week had resulted in the death of 15 people and caused widespread damage to infrastructure and crops in the coastal districts.
Heavy rains and strong winds caused extensive damage to infrastructure, including electricity networks and roads.
No untoward incident reported in Odisha due to cyclone, says Chief Secretary Anu Garg.
During the landfall process, winds gusting up to 90 kmph would prevail.

Railway services have been affected as a precaution against the expected weather conditions.

The cancellations include long-distance express services, Vande Bharat trains, passenger services and MEMU trains.
Passengers travelling through Puri, Bhubaneswar, Cuttack and Berhampur may face disruptions.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan: Heavy rain inundates low-lying areas of Ichchapuram, Sompeta in Srikakulam district
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan: Heavy rain inundates low-lying areas of Ichchapuram, Sompeta in Srikakulam district
stories.summary: Ichchapuram records 184.6 mm in 24 hours; the Collector says leave for all officials has been cancelled for relief work
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Srikakulam district has been witnessing heavy rain for the last day under the impact of Cyclone Akvan, which is yet to cross the coast between Ichchapuram in Andhra Pradesh and Gopalpur in Odisha.
The heavy rain inundated many low-lying areas of Ichchapuram, Kaviti, Sompeta and other places close to the sea coast of Srikakulam.
As per the latest data provided by the government, Srikakulam district recorded an average rainfall of 30.3 mm (908.4 mm across its mandals) between 8 a.m. on Thursday and 8 a.m. on Friday.
Ichchapuram received 184.6 mm, followed by Kanchili with 152 mm.
Kaviti got 149.2 mm and Sompeta 130.4 mm, throwing life out of gear for people of the Palasa division.
The district is likely to witness more downpours for the next two days, as per the precautionary guidelines given by the government and the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

Srikakulam Collector Swapnil Dinakar, who toured Ichchapuram and other places, said the situation was under control in the district, since many precautionary measures had been taken to mitigate the impact of the cyclone.
He said leave for all officials and staff had been cancelled so that they could take part in relief operations in Ichchapuram and other nearby mandals.
He said the Bahuda and other rivers might receive 30,000 cusecs of water because of heavy rain in their catchment areas in Odisha.
The district administration was coordinating closely with Odisha officials to monitor the flood situation, given the floods in the Bahuda a month ago, he said.
Mr. Swapnil said the enumeration of crop damage would be taken up in a few days.

Paryavarana Parirakshana Sangham leader and Jyotirao Phule Backward Classes Association State president Beena Dhilli Rao urged the government to appoint a high-level committee of experts and officials to study ways to protect people of Ichchapuram, Sompeta and other places that are regularly affected by natural calamities.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan to bring rain in Bihar; lightning alert issued
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan to bring rain in Bihar; lightning alert issued
stories.summary: This moisture-laden air is expected to contribute to cloud formation and rainfall across parts of the state.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: This moisture-laden air is expected to contribute to cloud formation and rainfall across parts of the state.
Patna: The impact of cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’, which has developed over the Bay of Bengal, is beginning to be felt in Bihar, with clouds covering several areas, including Patna, early on Friday.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast unsettled weather and light rainfall in several districts, along with a warning of lightning strikes.
According to the Meteorological Department, 13 districts may experience a change in weather conditions on Friday.
These include Patna, Nalanda, Jehanabad, Arwal, Gaya, Sheikhpura, Lakhisarai, Aurangabad, Jamui, Nawada, Banka, Bhagalpur and Munger.
Light rain is possible in these areas, while residents have been advised to remain cautious due to the possibility of lightning.
The weather is expected to remain unsettled in several parts of Bihar on November 21 and 22 as well, as the cyclonic system gradually influences weather conditions across eastern India.
The department has forecast light rainfall in Supaul, Araria, Kishanganj, Saharsa, Madhepura, Purnea, Katihar, Khagaria, Munger, Bhagalpur, Banka and Jamui during this period.
A warning of heavy rainfall has specifically been issued for Bhagalpur and Katihar.
Meteorologists said the system is likely to influence wind patterns over Bihar, bringing easterly winds carrying moisture from the Bay of Bengal.
According to the forecast, cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ is expected to move towards the vicinity of the Odisha and Andhra Pradesh coasts by Friday.
Wind speeds over the sea could reach 90-100 kmph, indicating the intensity of the weather system.

stories.title: Cyclone Akvan: Light rain in parts of Jharkhand; primary classes suspended in some districts
stories.summary: East Singhbhum and Saraikela-Kharswan district administrations have ordered schools to suspend primary classes on Friday (November 20, 2026) in view of the cyclone
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Parts of Jharkhand experienced light rainfall on Friday (November 20, 2026) morning under the influence of Cyclone Akvan as some district authorities suspended primary classes in schools, an official said.
The landfall process of the cyclone commenced near Gopalpur in Odisha around 8 a.m.

Rainfall is expected to intensify in the afternoon, as the IMD has issued an 'orange' alert (be prepared) for heavy downpour in five Jharkhand districts till 8.30 a.m. on Saturday (November 21, 2026), the official said.
East Singhbhum and Saraikela-Kharswan district administrations have ordered schools to suspend primary classes on Friday (November 20, 2026) in view of the cyclone.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an 'orange' alert for heavy rainfall in Dhanbad, Bokaro, Seraikela-Kharswan, and East and West Singhbhum districts till 8.30 a.m. on Saturday (November 21, 2026).
A 'yellow' alert (be updated) for heavy rain has been issued for Lohardaga, Gumla, Simdega, Ranchi, Khunti, Ramgarh and Jamtara for the same period, a weather bulletin said.
"The rainfall is likely to intensify later in the day and some districts may experience very heavy rainfall.
Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning are also likely in some places along with gusty winds of up to 50 kmph speed," Ranchi Meteorological Centre Deputy Director Abhishek Anand said.
He said the situation is expected to improve from November 22 and clear skies are likely from November 23.

stories.title: Cyclone Akvan triggers rain in south Bengal, IMD forecasts downpours till Saturday
stories.summary: Cyclone Akvan brings heavy rainfall to southern West Bengal, disrupting transport in Kolkata as the IMD issues warnings for coastal districts and advises fishermen to stay away from the sea until Saturday.
reasons: source: event has 3 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: wire echo (pti) -> no independent boost
article_sentences: Cyclone Akvan brings heavy rainfall to southern West Bengal, disrupting transport in Kolkata as the IMD issues warnings for coastal districts and advises fishermen to stay away from the sea until Saturday.
Kolkata: Cyclone Akvan triggered rain across several southern districts of West Bengal, with the IMD forecasting downpours in the region till Saturday.

The cyclonic storm, which made landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha, brought incessant light to moderate rain in Kolkata, leading to disruptions in public transport and causing inconvenience to office-goers during the morning peak hours on Friday.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast very heavy rain over the coastal districts of South 24 Parganas and Purba Medinipur till Saturday.
Several other districts of south Bengal will receive heavy rain till Saturday owing to the effect of the cyclone.
The Met office forecast light to moderate rain in Kolkata, with one or two spells of heavy rain on Friday.
The city received 19.2 mm of rainfall in 24 hours till 8.30 am on Friday, while Medinipur recorded the state's highest precipitation during the period at 47 mm, according to the IMD data.
The IMD advised fishermen not to venture into the sea along and off the West Bengal coast till Saturday, as sea conditions remain rough.

stories.headline: Meghalaya High Court Strikes Down Amendment To Maharam Syiem Election Law For Skipping Mandatory Re-Vote In Khasi Hills Council
stories.title: Meghalaya High Court Strikes Down Amendment To Maharam Syiem Election Law For Skipping Mandatory Re-Vote In Khasi Hills Council
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'strikes down' in title weight 40
article_sentences: The Meghalaya High Court has struck down the Khasi Hills Autonomous District (Nomination and Election of the Syiem, Deputy Syiem and Electors of Hima Maharam) (Amendment) Act, 2019, holding that the Khasi Hills Autonomous District Council (KHADC) could not incorporate substantive amendments to a Bill without placing them before the House for discussion and voting.

The Court observed that bypassing the mandatory legislative procedure under Rule 93 of the Assam and Meghalaya Autonomous Districts (Constitution of District Councils) Rules, 1951, amounted to a transgression of the Executive into the legislative domain of the Council.

Division Bench of Justice H.S. Thangkhiew and Justice B.Bhattacharjee remarked that: “The substantial amendments which were made, were not merely clerical..were never placed before the Chairman of the House for discussion or vote, which is a clear transgression of the executive into the legislative domain of the Council.”

The petitioners challenged the constitutional validity of the Khasi Hills Autonomous District (Nomination and Election of the Syiem, Deputy Syiem and Electors of Hima Maharam) (Amendment) Act, 2019, alleging that it was enacted without following the mandatory legislative procedure.

The Amendment Bill, passed by the Khasi Hills Autonomous District Council (KHADC) on July 25, 2019, proposed changes concerning the administration of Raid Saw Symper, including recognising the Myntri as the Rangbah Shnong (Headman) and prescribing a three-year tenure for the post.
Following objections raised by the Maharam Syiemship, the Bill was reconsidered and modified on the recommendations of the State Law Department.
However, the modified provisions were never placed before the Council for fresh discussion and voting before receiving the Governor's assent in September 2023.
The petitioners therefore challenged the Amendment Act for violating Rule 93 of the 1951 Rules.

The High Court held that Rule 93 of the Assam and Meghalaya Autonomous Districts (Constitution of District Councils) Rules, 1951, mandates that a Bill returned by the Governor for reconsideration must be placed before the District Council for discussion and voting before being resubmitted for assent.

The Court found that the 2019 Amendment Bill had been returned for reconsideration but the subsequent substantive changes recommended by the State Law Department were incorporated by the Executive Committee without being placed before the House.
It rejected the contention that the changes were merely clerical and held that such action amounted to an encroachment by the Executive into the legislative domain of the Council.
The Court observed that non-compliance with mandatory legislative procedure is open to judicial scrutiny.

stories.headline: Supreme Court declines plea for separate hearing on recall of split verdict in ECs’ appointment case
stories.title: Supreme Court declines plea for separate hearing on recall of split verdict in ECs’ appointment case
stories.summary: The CJI also said the five-judge Bench could consider the recall application even after the retirement of one of the judges who delivered the split verdict
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 20, 2026) declined a submission to separately list a plea seeking recall of a split verdict delivered by a two-judge bench on whether challenges to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners (ECs) should be referred to a larger bench.

A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said the recall application, as well as any challenge to the reference order, could be considered by the five-judge Constitution Bench already constituted to hear the batch of petitions challenging the validity of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.
The CJI also said the five-judge Bench could consider the recall application even after the retirement of one of the judges who delivered the split verdict.

Advocate Bhushan said that the recall application should be listed before the original bench comprising Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma, which delivered the split verdict on September 23.
He pointed out that Justice Sharma was due to retire next week.
Advocate Bhushan further said that Justice Sharma had a conflict of interest and, therefore, the application seeking recall of the verdict ought to be heard by the same bench.
When the CJI suggested that the reference bench could consider the application, Advocate Bhushan said the reference order itself was recalled on the ground of an alleged conflict of interest.
However, the CJI said that the issue could be raised before the five-judge Constitution bench, which has been constituted for final adjudication of the constitutional challenge to the 2023 law.
The development follows a split verdict delivered on September 23 by Justices Datta and Sharma on whether the petitions challenging the 2023 law warranted consideration by a larger bench.
The main objection was the exclusion of the CJI from the panel to select the CEC and ECs.
The panel now includes the prime minister, the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha and a cabinet minister.

While Justice Datta was of the view that the challenge could be adjudicated by a two-judge bench, Justice Sharma favoured a reference to a five-judge Constitution bench, considering the significant constitutional questions involved.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Directs Probe Into Why Registry Refused To List ED Plea Against Bail For Over Three Years
stories.title: Supreme Court Directs Probe Into Why Registry Refused To List ED Plea Against Bail For Over Three Years
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday(November 20) directed its Secretary General to conduct a fact-finding enquiry and submit a report explaining why a petition filed by the Enforcement Directorate in 2023 challenging a bail order was not listed for hearing for more than three years despite a judicial direction.

The bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing a petition filed by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) against the grant of bail to Raman Singla.
Notice in the matter had been issued in 2023, yet the case was never listed for over three years.
"Why has this matter not been listed?
September 2023, September 2024, September 2025, September 2026.
This is what I want to know," CJI Surya Kant asked at the outset.
Justice Bagchi described that situation as "institutional lethargy."

Senior Advocate Siddharth Dave, appearing for Singla, said that such a situation should not occur in the Supreme Court and that the Registry “can't be managed like that.” Dave remarked that he had “never seen this happen in the Supreme Court.”
"Maybe because you have not been in the Supreme Court Registry," retorted Senior Advocate Zoheb Hossain, who was representing the ED.
"I have been here twice the number of years you have practised, Mr Hossain," responded Dave.
"As an Advocate-on-Record I mean," Hossain clarified.
"Since 1990, I have been practising.

stories.headline: Assam Cabinet Approves Six New Municipal Boards, Land Allotment for Defence and Agricultural Institute
stories.title: Assam Cabinet Approves Six New Municipal Boards, Land Allotment for Defence and Agricultural Institute
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: GUWAHATI: The Assam Cabinet, which met in New Delhi today, took several decisions, including land allotment to the Ministry of Defence and expanding the areas of local urban bodies.
The cabinet has approved the allotment of 74 bighas of land in the Sonitpur district to the Ministry of Defence.
It also approved the allotment of 1,568 bighas of government land in Dhemaji for the setting up of an Indian Agriculture Research Institute.
To improve urban governance, the Cabinet has approved the creation of six new municipal boards, one each at Laluk, Harmutty-Bandardea, Ghilamara, Majuli, Udarbond, and Mirza-Bijay Nagar.
It also approved area expansion and ward delimitation in 23 existing urban local bodies.
The cabinet has approved classifying areas as urban areas only from 1 km from the town limits to facilitate larger land allocations for indigenous communities under Mission Basundhara 4.0.
This decision will not be applicable for the Kamrup (M) and Kamrup districts.
The cabinet has approved the enhancement of remuneration of the elected representatives of Panchayat Raj Institutes, Zila Parishad, Anchalik Parishads and Gaon Panchayats.
This will benefit presidents, vice-presidents and members of such bodies.

The cabinet has approved the amendment of the Matak Autonomous Council Act, the Kamatapur Autonomous Council Act, and the Moran Autonomous Council Act for conducting elections to the general councils of these autonomous councils on a non-political party basis.

stories.headline: Ahead of demolition, Army Welfare Housing Organisation begins takeover of Chander Kunj flats in Kochi
stories.title: Ahead of demolition, Army Welfare Housing Organisation begins takeover of Chander Kunj flats in Kochi
stories.summary: Last month, a Single Bench of Kerala High Court directed AWHO to take possession of apartments from residents and hand them over to Edifice Engineering, company entrusted with the demolition work
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Army Welfare Housing Organisation (AWHO) has begun taking over apartments in Chander Kunj Army Towers ‘B’ and ‘C’ at Silver Sand Island, Vyttila, in Kochi, ahead of their demolition.

A Single Bench of the Kerala High Court had last month directed the AWHO to take possession of the apartments from the residents and hand them over to Edifice Engineering, the company entrusted with the demolition work.

The takeover, originally scheduled to begin on October 5, 2026, and be completed within a fortnight, as decided by a committee headed by the District Collector, was stalled after the AWHO challenged the decision in the High Court.
Apartment owners from across the State had turned up to hand over their flats in response to a notice issued by the apartment association, but could not do so.
“We have issued fresh notices to apartment owners regarding the takeover.
However, the actual demolition can begin only after the demolition contract with Edifice Engineering is finalised.

The district administration has shared a revised draft agreement, which is likely to be finalised at the next meeting of the Collector’s committee,” said Saji Thomas, president of the Chander Kunj Army Towers Apartment Owners Association (CATAOA).
The apartments are being taken over in the presence of the Kanayannur tahsildar before being handed over to Edifice Engineering.
More than 20 apartment owners who have shifted to rented accommodation turned up to hand over the keys to their flats.

The AWHO has already taken possession of around 50 apartments belonging to owners who opted for the buy-back option instead of receiving newly constructed apartments in replacement for the demolished ones.

Originally, the plan was to hand over the apartment keys along with an affidavit signed by the AWHO and countersigned by the tahsildar, affirming the organisation’s undertaking to provide reconstructed apartments in place of the existing ones.
However, this arrangement was dropped on Friday.

stories.headline: India poised to get preferential trade access to $85 trillion of global GDP: Piyush Goyal
stories.title: India poised to get preferential trade access to $85 trillion of global GDP: Piyush Goyal
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: New Delhi: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Thursday that India will have preferential trade access to $85 trillion of global GDP by next year, up from $70 trillion at present, as ongoing trade negotiations add another $15 trillion.
He also noted that several trade agreements, including a deal with the US, are expected to be finalised in the coming months.

Addressing FICCI's annual general meeting here, the minister reiterated India's push toward its $1 trillion overall export target for FY27, urging businesses and startups to tap global market opportunities.
"We didn't know how the year would pan out.
Two global wars are raging even today as we speak.
But when you really desire something from the heart, it can happen," Goyal remarked.
He pointed out that India's export figure of $90 billion for October was "an all-time high."
Delivering the valedictory keynote address, titled "India's Growth Imperative: Building a Globally Competitive Economy," the minister said, "We need to make the world dependent upon us.
We have to create leverage in India."
India has the capabilities, the talent, capital, entrepreneurs, and skill sets.
The country has robust economic fundamentals to move forward and a strong banking ecosystem to meet the higher ambition level, the minister stated.
"We have got an economy that matters.
